summary: Updates the IETF's rules on rights in contributions (RFC 3978) to say that the IETF Trust is now the proper holder of IETF-related intellectual property rights. It does not limit how the Trust uses them. This is a Best Current Practice and was replaced by RFC 5378.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4748 updates the contribution-rights rules in RFC 3978 to recognize the IETF Trust as custodian of IETF-related intellectual property. It makes the Trust the recipient of the specified license grants and was later replaced by RFC 5378.

questions: who receives ietf contribution license grants
subtitle: Updates the IETF contribution-rights document to recognize the IETF Trust.

tldr.problem: RFC 3978 needed to reflect that the IETF Trust had become the administrative custodian of intellectual-property rights related to the IETF Standards Process.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4748 makes targeted text changes in RFC 3978, including changing the license-grant path so contributors grant licenses to the IETF Trust.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4748 updated RFC 3978 and was later obsoleted by RFC 5378.

today: RFC 4748 updated RFC 3978 and has been obsoleted by RFC 5378.

sections.title: Recognizing the IETF Trust
sections.content:
RFC 3978 describes rights and permissions that authors grant when contributing to the IETF Standards Process. The IETF Trust was formed to act as administrative custodian of copyrights and other intellectual-property rights related to that process, rights previously held by ISOC and CNRI.

RFC 4748 updates RFC 3978 to recognize the Trust and put the structure needed to support it into the contribution-rights text.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF Trust was created to manage rights related to IETF standards work. This update changes RFC 3978 to name the Trust in the relevant rules.

sections.title: Changes to the License Grant
sections.content:
The most important change is to the license-grant path. Where RFC 3978 said authors grant a license to ISOC, RFC 4748 changes the text so authors grant a license to the IETF Trust.

The document also updates references to ISOC and the Internet Society in specific sections of RFC 3978, its copyright statement, and related provisions. It says it is concerned only with changes needed to recognize the Trust.
sections.plainLanguage: The update changes who receives the license grant: the IETF Trust instead of ISOC. It makes corresponding edits to references elsewhere in RFC 3978.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says this process document has no direct impact on the security of the Internet or Internet protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: The document changes process rules and says it has no direct effect on Internet or protocol security.
